text: nosuggests platform report ERROR vignette re-building vignette uses rmarkdown engine (immunogenetr’s ): real CRAN blocker — CRAN’s incoming check runs _R_CHECK_FORCE_SUGGESTS_=false, downgrades exact case NOTE. code: Error: processing vignette 'immunogenetr.Rmd' failed with diagnostics: there is no package called 'rmarkdown' ## R-hub notes  The `nosuggests` platform reports an ERROR at "checking re-building of vignette outputs":      Error: processing vignette 'immunogenetr.Rmd' failed with diagnostics:     there is no package called 'rmarkdown'  This is the standard interaction between R-hub's `nosuggests` platform and vignettes built with the `rmarkdown` engine. title: Getting Started with immunogenetr
text: Clinical HLA data typically stored tabular format, allele column. immunogenetr includes HLA_typing_1 dataset example: HLA_columns_to_GLstring() function converts columns single GL String per individual. used inside mutate(), pass . first argument reference working data frame: GL String encodes full genotype: alleles within gene copy separated / (ambiguity), gene copies +, loci ^.
code: # HLA_typing_1 contains typing for 10 individuals across all classical HLA loci. head(HLA_typing_1, 3) HLA_typing_GL <- HLA_typing_1 %>%   # Convert all typing columns (A1 through DPB1_2) into a GL String.   mutate(     GL_string = HLA_columns_to_GLstring(., HLA_typing_columns = A1:DPB1_2),     .after = patient   ) %>%   # Keep only patient ID and the new GL String column.   select(patient, GL_string)  # View the GL Strings. (HLA_typing_GL)

code: # Patient 7 is the recipient, patient 9 is the donor. recip_gl <- HLA_typing_GL %>% filter(patient == 7) %>% pull(GL_string) donor_gl <- HLA_typing_GL %>% filter(patient == 9) %>% pull(GL_string)

text: HLA_match_summary_HCT() function provides standard match grades used hematopoietic cell transplantation:
code: # X-of-8 matching (A, B, C, DRB1 bidirectional). HLA_match_summary_HCT(recip_gl, donor_gl,   direction = "bidirectional",   match_grade = "Xof8" ) #> [1] 1 # X-of-10 matching (adds DQB1). HLA_match_summary_HCT(recip_gl, donor_gl,   direction = "bidirectional",   match_grade = "Xof10" ) #> [1] 1

title: Getting Started with immunogenetr
text: common workflow comparing one recipient multiple potential donors:
code: # Patient 3 is the recipient; compare against all 10 donors. recipient <- HLA_typing_GL %>%   filter(patient == 3) %>%   select(GL_string) %>%   rename(GL_string_recip = GL_string)  donors <- HLA_typing_GL %>%   rename(GL_string_donor = GL_string, donor = patient) %>%   # Cross-join to pair recipient with each donor.   cross_join(recipient) %>%   # Calculate 8/8 match grade for each pair.   mutate(     match_8of8 = HLA_match_summary_HCT(       GL_string_recip, GL_string_donor,       direction = "bidirectional",       match_grade = "Xof8"     ),     .after = donor   ) %>%   # Sort best matches first.   arrange(desc(match_8of8))  donors %>% select(donor, match_8of8)

text: HLA_truncate() reduces allele resolution specified number fields:
code: # Truncate a four-field allele to two fields. HLA_truncate("HLA-A*02:01:01:01", fields = 2) #> [1] "HLA-A*02:01" # Works on full GL Strings too. HLA_truncate("HLA-A*02:01:01:01+HLA-A*03:01:01:02^HLA-B*07:02:01:01+HLA-B*44:02:01:01",   fields = 2 ) #> [1] "HLA-A*02:01+HLA-A*03:01^HLA-B*07:02+HLA-B*44:02"

title: Getting Started with immunogenetr
text: HLA_prefix_remove() HLA_prefix_add() manage HLA- locus prefixes:
code: # Remove all prefixes to get just the allele fields. HLA_prefix_remove("HLA-A*02:01") #> [1] "02:01" # Keep the locus designation but remove "HLA-". HLA_prefix_remove("HLA-A*02:01", keep_locus = TRUE) #> [1] "A*02:01" # Add the full prefix back. HLA_prefix_add("02:01", "HLA-A*") #> [1] "HLA-A*02:01" # "HLA-" is added by default. HLA_prefix_add("A*02:01") #> [1] "HLA-A*02:01"

title: Getting Started with immunogenetr
text: GLstring_regex() creates regex patterns accurately search within GL strings, preventing partial matches across field boundaries: Expression suffixes G/P groups handled simple rule: search without suffix matches allele regardless expression status group membership, search carrying suffix matches alleles letter, higher resolution. G P group search matches group name , member alleles: matched text always full allele appears GL String, stringr::str_extract() reports actually found: HLA- prefix optional allele GL String — wild-caught GL Strings often omit — allele either convention matches GL String either convention:
code: gl <- "HLA-A*02:01:01+HLA-A*68:01^HLA-B*07:01+HLA-B*15:01"  # A two-field search correctly matches the three-field allele. pattern <- GLstring_regex("HLA-A*02:01") stringr::str_detect(gl, pattern) #> [1] TRUE # But won't falsely match a longer allele number. stringr::str_detect("HLA-A*02:149:01", GLstring_regex("HLA-A*02:14")) #> [1] FALSE # An unsuffixed search finds the null allele. stringr::str_detect("HLA-A*24:09N+HLA-A*02:01", GLstring_regex("HLA-A*24:09")) #> [1] TRUE # A null search finds the null allele at higher resolution, but never an # expressed allele. stringr::str_detect("HLA-A*01:01:03N", GLstring_regex("HLA-A*01:01N")) #> [1] TRUE stringr::str_detect("HLA-A*01:01:03", GLstring_regex("HLA-A*01:01N")) #> [1] FALSE stringr::str_extract(gl, GLstring_regex("HLA-A*02:01")) #> [1] "HLA-A*02:01:01" stringr::str_detect("A*02:01:01+A*68:01", GLstring_regex("HLA-A*02:01")) #> [1] TRUE stringr::str_extract(gl, GLstring_regex("A*02:01")) #> [1] "HLA-A*02:01:01"

title: Getting Started with immunogenetr
text: unsuffixed search matches expression variants, workflows ignore non-expressed alleles can remove first GLstring_drop_non_expressed(). default removes N, S C alleles, produce cell-surface protein; suffixes argument adjusts judgement:
code: # The null allele is removed; a gene copy or locus with nothing left collapses # cleanly. GLstring_drop_non_expressed("HLA-A*01:01N+HLA-A*02:01^HLA-B*07:02/HLA-B*07:02N+HLA-B*08:01") #> [1] "HLA-A*02:01^HLA-B*07:02+HLA-B*08:01" # Remove only null alleles. GLstring_drop_non_expressed("HLA-A*01:01N+HLA-A*23:38S", suffixes = "N") #> [1] "HLA-A*23:38S"

title: Getting Started with immunogenetr
text: working tidyverse, column names dashes asterisks inconvenient. HLA_column_repair() converts -standard (HLA-*) tidyverse-friendly (HLA_A) formats:
code: # GLstring_genes returns tidyverse-friendly names by default. repaired <- GLstring_genes(single_patient, "GL_string") names(repaired) #> [1] "HLA_A"    "HLA_C"    "HLA_B"    "HLA_DRB5" "HLA_DRB1" "HLA_DQA1" "HLA_DQB1" #> [8] "HLA_DPA1" "HLA_DPB1" # Convert back to WHO format with asterisks. who_names <- HLA_column_repair(repaired, format = "WHO", asterisk = TRUE) names(who_names) #> [1] "HLA-A*"    "HLA-C*"    "HLA-B*"    "HLA-DRB5*" "HLA-DRB1*" "HLA-DQA1*" #> [7] "HLA-DQB1*" "HLA-DPA1*" "HLA-DPB1*"

code: library(immunogenetr) library(tidyverse)  # The "HLA_typing_1" dataset is installed with immunogenetr, and contains high resolution typing at all classical # HLA loci for ten individuals.  kable_hla(HLA_typing_1) HLA_typing_1_GLstring <- HLA_typing_1 %>%   mutate(GL_string = HLA_columns_to_GLstring(., HLA_typing_columns = A1:DPB1_2), .after = patient) %>%   # Note the syntax for the `HLA_columns_to_GLstring` arguments - when this function is used inside   # of a `mutate` function to make a new column in a data frame, "." is used in the first argument   # to tell the function to use the working data frame as the source of the HLA typing columns.   select(patient, GL_string)  kable_hla(HLA_typing_1_GLstring) # Select one case each for recipient and donor. HLA_typing_1_GLstring_recipient <- HLA_typing_1_GLstring %>%   filter(patient == 7) %>%   rename(GL_string_recipient = GL_string, case = patient)  HLA_typing_1_GLstring_donor <- HLA_typing_1_GLstring %>%   filter(patient == 9) %>%   rename(GL_string_donor = GL_string) %>%   select(-patient)  # Combine the tables so recipient and donor are on the same row. HLA_typing_1_recip_donor <- bind_cols(   HLA_typing_1_GLstring_recipient,   HLA_typing_1_GLstring_donor   )  kable_hla(HLA_typing_1_recip_donor) HLA_typing_1_recip_donor_mismatches <- HLA_typing_1_recip_donor %>%   mutate(A_MM_GvH = HLA_mismatch_logical(                       GL_string_recipient,                       GL_string_donor,                       "HLA-A",                       direction = "GvH"),                     .after = case) %>%   mutate(A_MM_HvG = HLA_mismatch_logical(                       GL_string_recipient,                       GL_string_donor,                       "HLA-A",                       direction = "HvG"),                     .after = A_MM_GvH)  kable_hla(HLA_typing_1_recip_donor_mismatches) HLA_typing_1_recip_donor_mismatched_allles <- HLA_typing_1_recip_donor %>%   mutate(A_HvG_MMs = HLA_mismatched_alleles(                         GL_string_recipient,                         GL_string_donor,                         "HLA-A",                         direction = "HvG"),                       .after = case)  kable_hla(HLA_typing_1_recip_donor_mismatched_allles) # Determine the number of bidirectional mismatches at several loci. HLA_typing_1_recip_donor_MM_number <- HLA_typing_1_recip_donor %>%   mutate(ABCDRB1_MM = HLA_mismatch_number(                         GL_string_recipient,                         GL_string_donor,                         c("HLA-A", "HLA-B", "HLA-C", "HLA-DRB1"),                         direction = "bidirectional"),                       .after = case)  kable_hla(HLA_typing_1_recip_donor_MM_number) # The match_grade argument of "Xof8" will return the number of matches at the HLA-A, B, C, and DRB1 loci. HLA_typing_1_recip_donor_8of8_matching <- HLA_typing_1_recip_donor %>%   mutate(ABCDRB1_matching = HLA_match_summary_HCT(                               GL_string_recipient,                               GL_string_donor,                               direction = "bidirectional",                               match_grade = "Xof8"),                             .after = case)  kable_hla(HLA_typing_1_recip_donor_8of8_matching) # Select one case to be the recipient. HLA_typing_1_GLstring_candidate <- HLA_typing_1_GLstring %>%   filter(patient == 3) %>%   select(GL_string) %>%   rename(GL_string_recip = GL_string)  # Join the recipient to the 10-donor list and perform matching HLA_typing_1_GLstring_donors <- HLA_typing_1_GLstring %>%   rename(GL_string_donor = GL_string, donor = patient) %>%   cross_join(HLA_typing_1_GLstring_candidate) %>%   mutate(ABCDRB1_matching = HLA_match_summary_HCT(                               GL_string_recip,                               GL_string_donor,                               direction = "bidirectional",                               match_grade = "Xof8"),                             .after = donor) %>%   arrange(desc(ABCDRB1_matching))  kable_hla(HLA_typing_1_GLstring_donors)

title: GLstring_drop_non_expressed — GLstring_drop_non_expressed
text: function removes alleles carrying expression suffix GL String. default suffixes N (null), S (secreted) C (cytoplasmic) removed, reasoning alleles produce protein cell surface; L (low), Q (questionable) (aberrant) alleles kept, surface expression possible. suffixes treat non-expressed clinical judgement, `suffixes` argument can set combination six. title: GLstring_regex — GLstring_regex
text: function format HLA allele (e.g. "HLA-*02:01") regex pattern searching within GL String. allele must carry locus designation, "HLA-" prefix optional allele GL String searched: "*02:01" "HLA-*02:01" produce equivalent patterns, either matches allele whether GL String writes without prefix (wild-caught GL Strings often omit ). bare field value locus ("02:01") rejected, since locus inferred; `HLA_prefix_add` function useful repairing values. pattern matches whole alleles , rules: * allele supplied fewer fields match higher-resolution allele   GL String ("HLA-*02:01" matches "HLA-*02:01:01:01"), partial   fields never match ("HLA-*02:14" match "HLA-*02:149"). * allele without expression suffix matches regardless expression   status: "HLA-*24:09" matches "HLA-*24:09N". likewise matches G P   group names, include allele name ("HLA-*01:01:01"   matches "HLA-*01:01:01G"). * allele supplied expression suffix (N, Q, L, S, C )   G/P group letter matches alleles carrying letter,   higher resolution: "HLA-*01:01N" matches "HLA-*01:01:03N"   "HLA-*01:01:03" "HLA-*01:01:03Q". Note G P group query   matches group name written GL String;   expand group's member alleles ("HLA-*01:01:01G" match   "HLA-*01:01:01" "HLA-*01:32"), since group membership defined   IPD-IMGT/HLA database rather allele name. find   member group, search base allele name instead. matched text always full allele name appears GL String, `stringr::str_extract` returns allele found (search string), `stringr::str_replace` replaces whole allele.

code: # To understand how the function works we can see how it alters the allele "HLA-A*02:01":  GLstring_regex("HLA-A*02:01") #> [1] "(?:(?<=[\\?\\^\\|\\+\\~/])|^)(HLA-)?A\\*02:01(:\\d+)*[NQLSCAGP]?(?=(\\?|\\^|\\||\\+|\\~|/|$))"  # The result is the same allele with extra formatting to escape special characters found # in a GL String, as well as the ability to accurately search for an allele in a GL String. # For example, we would not want the allele "HLA-A*02:14" to match to "HLA-A*02:149:01", # which would happen if we simply escaped the special characters:  library(stringr) str_view("HLA-A*02:149:01", str_escape("HLA-A*02:14"), match = NA) #> [1] │ <HLA-A*02:14>9:01  # Using `GLstring_regex` prevents this:  str_view("HLA-A*02:149:01", GLstring_regex("HLA-A*02:14"), match = NA) #> [1] │ HLA-A*02:149:01  # Using a longer GL String with multiple alleles and loci:  GL_string <- "HLA-A*02:01:01+HLA-A*68:01^HLA-B*07:01+HLA-B*15:01"  # We can match any allele accurately:  str_view(GL_string, GLstring_regex("HLA-A*68:01"), match = NA) #> [1] │ HLA-A*02:01:01+<HLA-A*68:01>^HLA-B*07:01+HLA-B*15:01  # Note that alleles supplied with fewer fields than in the GL String will also match, # and that the match is the full allele as written in the GL String:  str_view(GL_string, GLstring_regex("HLA-A*02:01"), match = NA) #> [1] │ <HLA-A*02:01:01>+HLA-A*68:01^HLA-B*07:01+HLA-B*15:01  # An allele without an expression suffix matches its expression variants:  str_view("HLA-A*24:09N+HLA-A*02:01", GLstring_regex("HLA-A*24:09"), match = NA) #> [1] │ <HLA-A*24:09N>+HLA-A*02:01  # An allele with an expression suffix matches only alleles carrying that suffix, # at the same or higher resolution:  str_view("HLA-A*01:01:03N+HLA-A*02:01", GLstring_regex("HLA-A*01:01N"), match = NA) #> [1] │ <HLA-A*01:01:03N>+HLA-A*02:01 str_view("HLA-A*01:01:03Q+HLA-A*02:01", GLstring_regex("HLA-A*01:01N"), match = NA) #> [1] │ HLA-A*01:01:03Q+HLA-A*02:01  # The "HLA-" prefix is optional in both the allele and the GL String, so a # canonical allele finds its match in a wild-caught GL String without prefixes, # and vice versa:  str_view("A*02:01:01+A*68:01", GLstring_regex("HLA-A*02:01"), match = NA) #> [1] │ <A*02:01:01>+A*68:01 str_view("HLA-A*02:01:01+HLA-A*68:01", GLstring_regex("A*02:01"), match = NA) #> [1] │ <HLA-A*02:01:01>+HLA-A*68:01

One allele per cell function's contract: cell holding GL String reduced first allele (see `take_first_allele`). HLA_typing_columns list columns containing HLA alleles. Relabeling structural : `"ser"` strips asterisk uses serologic locus name; `"mol"` uses molecular locus name. cross-nomenclature allele translation performed. take_first_allele logical value, passed `HLA_validate` cell cleaned. TRUE (default), cell containing GL String delimiters ("^", "|", "+", "~", "/" "?") silently reduced first allele. text: CRAN release: 2026-05-26 Rewrote HLA_prefix_remove skip GL String expand--reassemble round-trip. previous implementation expanded GL String ambiguity tibble, ran str_replace , reassembled — dominant cost pipeline called HLA_prefix_remove per cell. Now four direct regex passes GL String character vector. ~100× faster end--end, ~420× less memory allocated 100,000-input workloads. many functions package (including HLA_columns_to_GLstring) call HLA_prefix_remove internally, every downstream caller picks speedup free. End--end ~68× faster 1000 rows (7.4 s -> 109 ms) ~200× faster 10,000 rows (~272 s -> ~1.3 s). Rewrote HLA_mismatch_base replace per-pair purrr::map2_chr loop stringr wrappers base-R / stringi primitives, hoist invariants per-pair loop, short-circuit null-allele regex alleles match. ~26× faster 100 pairs, ~11× faster 10,000 pairs, ~1000× less memory allocated large workload. Also tuned residual unify_locus / DRB3/4/5 classification / molecular prefix extraction hot spots exposed post-merge re-profile. Rewrote four HLA_mismatch_* derivatives (HLA_mismatch_logical, HLA_mismatch_number, HLA_mismatch_alleles, HLA_mismatched_alleles) replace shared tibble -> separate_longer_delim -> separate_wider_delim -> summarise post-processing pipeline direct character-vector ops integer mismatch count matrix. 10-50× less memory; 10-15% faster per call (underlying HLA_mismatch_base call now dominates). Rewrote HLA_match_number HLA_match_summary_HCT share new internal helper hla_mismatch_count_matrix() exposes integer count matrix HLA_mismatch_number already builds, skipping format--reparse round-trip string output. 15-20% faster end--end, 10-21× less memory per call. Rewrote GLstring_expand_longer replace 7-level tidyr::separate_longer_delim + row_number() chain stringi::stri_split_fixed cascade assembles output tibble directly equal-length index vectors. 20-43× faster depending input size; 4× less memory. Rewrote ambiguity_table_to_GLstring replace six chained dplyr::summarise(str_flatten(...)) passes single sort--paste helper. Subsequent levels GL hierarchy skip redundant sort since composite index key stays sorted prefix truncation. 2-13× faster depending size remove_duplicates flag. Rewrote HLA_truncate replace GLstring_expand_longer -> 4x separate_wider_delim -> 4x unite -> ambiguity_table_to_GLstring pipeline vectorised per-allele truncator flattens fields across alleles single long vector regex processing, collapses per allele one pass. ~5× faster end--end 1000 alleles. title: immunogenetr 1.1.0
text: CRAN release: 2026-04-07 Internal code quality improvements: fixed typos internal variable names, corrected test filenames, cleaned globalVariables() declarations. Standardized error messages use cli_abort() consistent, informative error reporting across package. Bumped cli dependency >= 3.0.0. Added input validation exported functions. Functions now check NULL, wrong types, invalid parameter values processing, providing clear error messages instead cryptic failures. Added internal validation helper functions (check_gl_string, check_data_frame, check_loci, check_logical_flag, check_homozygous_count, check_fields). Added match.arg() validation match_grade direction parameters HLA_match_summary_HCT. Refactored duplicated matching logic across HLA_match_summary_HCT, HLA_match_number, HLA_mismatch_number, HLA_mismatch_logical. Replaced repeated direction-branching code blocks parameterized pipelines, significantly reducing code duplication changes behavior. Optimized HLA_mismatch_base: consolidated duplicated GvH/HvG mismatch calculation single parameterized code path, eliminated repeated strsplit() calls within mismatch loop, extracted duplicated locus-naming logic shared helper function. Optimized HLA_mismatch_number HLA_mismatch_logical compute requested direction(s). Previously functions always computed GvH HvG regardless requested direction; now HvG, GvH, SOT requests compute single direction, cutting HLA_mismatch_base calls half. Bidirectional requests still compute needed. Also extracted duplicated multi-locus table-building code internal helper functions. Expanded test coverage HLA_mismatch_logical, HLA_match_number, HLA_mismatched_alleles using mismatch_table_2010 mismatch_table_2016 consensus reference tables, matching existing comprehensive table-based tests HLA_mismatch_number. Optimized HLA_columns_to_GLstring: replaced 16 case-insensitive regex calls locus detection single tolower() plus startsWith() lookups (~7.5x faster), replaced serologic name case_when named vector lookup (~37x faster), combined multiple str_detect() calls molecular typing detection single patterns. Optimized HLA_truncate: replaced four nearly-identical /else blocks field selection parameterized approach using computed keep_cols/drop_cols vectors, reducing code duplication improving maintainability. Optimized ambiguity_table_to_GLstring: extracted collapse_level() helper function replace six repetitions conditional distinct() + summarise() pattern, significantly reducing code duplication. Optimized GLstring_genotype_ambiguity: simplified gene-separator error detection multi-step pipeline single vectorized check, combined two separate str_replace() + na_if() calls one operation. Expanded test coverage HLA_column_repair, GLstring_genes, GLstring_regex, read_HML comprehensive tests covering format conversions, parameter combinations, edge cases, input validation, error handling. Fixed read_HML dynamically discover XML namespace instead hardcoding d1: prefix. function now uses xml_ns() detect namespace file, improving compatibility HML files different sources. Fixed null allele detection regex HLA_mismatch_base support locus names longer 4 characters (e.g. HLA-DRB345). lookbehind now allows 10 alphanumeric characters HLA-. Added “Getting Started” vignette covering major workflows: tabular--GL String conversion, locus splitting, mismatch/match calculation, allele name utilities, HML file reading. Added package-level help page (?immunogenetr) organizing exported functions datasets category. Added inst/CITATION file package publication: Coskun & Brown (2026), “Immunogenetr: comprehensive toolkit clinical HLA informatics,” Human Immunology, 87(1):111619. doi:10.1016/j.humimm.2025.111619.
